$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.16,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.16/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 8c5b2cb0df808eed2ee6cc4948f7398d721f6400e5d024b222f1772f8ae26048 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.16/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
8c5b2cb0df808eed2ee6cc4948f7398d721f6400e5d024b222f1772f8ae26048 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
